notes:
Snapshot: Mid-market multi-tenant SaaS (agent platform) evaluating Redwood as a primary LLM inference provider. Current path: start with Hosted API POC (fast time-to-value) → if SLOs and cost profile acceptable, move to Dedicated reserved capacity for predictable per-tenant QoS and VPC requirements.

Key requirements / ask from Aurora: 
- Workload: low-latency conversational agents with tool calling (web fetch, DB reads) and streaming responses to clients.
- Latency targets: 95th percentile end-to-end for streaming tokens <= 250ms for single-turn small responses; tail for long responses acceptable up to 400ms, but customer prefers 200-250ms for critical flows.
- Throughput: multi-tenant environment: ~120 active tenants, expected concurrency per tenant 10-15 simultaneous sessions (peaks up to 150 concurrent sessions), average tokens per request ~120, burst QPS observed ~80 across cluster during POC.
- Operational: enforce per-tenant quotas and rate limits (soft limits per minute + stricter burst controls), token-based billing breakdown per tenant, support for graceful degradation (fallback to smaller model variant or rate-limited responses).
- Security/compliance: require SOC2 attestation, SSO/SAML integration, audit logs for generation events, optional KMS for encryption, potential EU data residency for some customers.
- Integration: needs streaming SDK stability (client reconnects, resume on transient drops) and deterministic tool-calling hooks with idempotency.

POC results & observations: 
- Hosted API POC passed basic correctness and tool-calling tests. 
- Latency: average latency looks good (~120-180ms for small responses) but 95p spikes to ~420ms under burst scenarios — key concern.
- Streaming: observed occasional chunk drops when concurrent bursts increased; SE opened INF-4321 to investigate keepalive, chunking strategy, and client-side reconnection recommendations.
- Rate-limits: need fine-grained tenant-level throttles; current hosted tier rate limits caused noisy neighbors during synthetic tests. Aurora asked about per-tenant isolated rate limit groups or token-bucket per api-key backed by Dedicated capacity.
- Cost: fairly cost-sensitive; prefers Optimize suggestions (batching + quantization) if moving to Dedicated.

Quotes / snippets: 
- "We need predictable tail latency — our SLAs to enterprise customers hinge on 95p latency for streaming UX." — Product lead
- "If Hosted can’t guarantee per-tenant isolation, we’ll need Dedicated or on-prem options." — CTO

Next steps (short): 
- Provide Dedicated 6-month and 12-month pricing scenarios with expected unit economics at target SLOs.
- Deliver network/VPC diagram and guide for Dedicated deployment.
- SE to share tuned streaming config and client-side best practices (retry/resume) — target demo 2026-03-10.
- Legal to receive template DPA focused on EU residency requirements.

Longer term: Aurora likely to prefer Dedicated if Redwood demonstrates predictable tail behavior and per-tenant quotas. Opportunity to sell Optimize addon and longer term Reserved capacity with rollout assistance and extended SLAs.
